neighbours.label: 'the (total) number of X' used as a counted measure: fires on ' number' / ' of' / ' total' when a quantity is defined or tallied as a count of items (opposite pole: a person's age)
fire: The flood on Friday pushed the total number of homes evacuated this month above three thousand.
The order of a group is the number of elements that it contains.
Last night's game raised the total number of goals scored this season to ninety.
The length of a path is the number of edges that it crosses.
The new outbreak brings the total number of confirmed cases above five hundred.
The dimension of the space is the number of vectors required to span it.
The app measures activity by the number of steps taken during each hour.
Yesterday's arrests took the total number of suspects held in the case to eleven.
quiet: The flood on Friday pushed muddy water through the homes along the river.
The order of a group is the first property that students learn about.
Last night's game raised the hopes of supporters who had waited all season.
The length of a path is hard to judge when the fog is thick.
The new outbreak brings fresh worries for the hospitals in the region.
The dimension of the room is the reason the piano would not fit.
The app measures activity by tracking the phone's movement during each hour.
Yesterday's arrests took the neighbourhood by surprise, and her phone number was leaked.

short: 'the number of X' as a count
